The project is called Artcraft, and the developer's name is Brandon Thomas, who after being hit with Adobe's cancellation fee more than once, opened up Claude, then reverse engineered Adobe's 30 plus year codebase from scratch, and the apps even run on Linux, a platform Adobe is never officially supported. What's crazy though is that you, the human being watching this video, can do the same thing thanks to an unrelated project called Reverse Engineer Anything. It's been going viral on the internet lately because it can easily decompile any native binaries you can get your hands on. We're talking stripped ELF PE and MCCO executables, JVM bite code with obuscated constant pools, ECMA 335 compliant assemblies, bare metal firmware with architecture specific instruction sets, and even OCI container layers entangled in declarative infrastructure manifests. In layman's terms, that means virtually every app in the world is now open source, whether it wants to be or not.
